cand.title: FMF200: The Future of Mathematical Finance
cand.organizationName: University of Toronto Department of Statistical Sciences

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two relevant contact candidates, neither a verified hotel-contract buyer: Sebastian Jaimungal, Department Chair and professor, publicly announced FMF200; approach for an introduction to whoever coordinates invited-speaker travel and accommodation. Kal Romain, Manager, Media & Communications, is a departmental operational routing contact: the department associates him with communications inquiries and the edition directs registration/conference questions to that function. His event-specific hotel responsibilities are unverified.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced activity dates: May 26–28, 2027, University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. This edition is upcoming as of November 16, 2026 and within the requested horizon. Registration is open; these are conference dates, not publication dates. No subsequent edition through June 2028 was located.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel brief: conditional lodging-only fit for a modest subset of nonlocal delegates or invited speakers at the 157-room Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown. The conference remains at 700 University Avenue; meeting-space displacement is not evidenced. Harbourfront positioning does not confer the same convenience as lodging near the university venue, and MTCC walkability is not an event-specific advantage here. Attendance, nonlocal share and room demand are unpublished, so neither group size nor a 15–109-room block is established. No resort requirement is indicated. Do not pitch catering or receptions until restaurant/lounge and service capability are verified.
findings.venueCommitments: Published conference location: University of Toronto, 700 University Avenue, 9th Floor, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. The departmental directory identifies this address as the Ontario Power Building. Toronto proper / downtown university area, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. No specific auditorium or meeting-room name is published. This is an official venue announcement, not evidence of a hotel contract or independently inspected venue agreement.
findings.historicalRotation: No prior FMF200 edition or destination/venue rotation was identified. The official event is explicitly tied to the University of Toronto bicentennial. Annual recurrence and a 2028 edition are not established; do not substitute unrelated mathematical-finance conferences as predecessors.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. No edition-specific hotel, room block, housing bureau, host hotel, open lodging RFP or booking commitment was found on the official home, registration and call-for-papers pages. Hotels listed for this edition: none found. The registration page states: “For questions about conference registration, please contact: communications.statistics@utoronto.ca”. This establishes an inquiry route, not a lodging-sourcing pathway. No source statement describing housing arrangements was located to quote.
findings.organizationStructure: University-hosted academic event, owned/hosted publicly by the University of Toronto Department of Statistical Sciences. Not evidenced as an association convention or agency-owned event. No external PCO, DMC, housing bureau or contracted accommodation buyer was identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No incumbent hotel, exclusive block, sell-out, overflow requirement or competitive lodging commitment was verified. Generic university hotel lists are not FMF200 commitments and are excluded. Inference: the separate university venue makes location/convenience a sales consideration for a Harbourfront hotel. Event size is unknown, so it cannot responsibly be classified as too large or too small for this hotel.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Send a concise accommodation-qualification inquiry to communications.statistics@utoronto.ca, addressed to Kal Romain, and seek Sebastian Jaimungal’s referral to the travel/lodging coordinator. Ask whether invited speakers or delegates need hotel rooms, who pays and contracts, whether any hotel/bureau is appointed, booking dates, expected nonlocal attendance, peak rooms, budget and transit preferences. Offer a modest rooms-only proposal only after an unmet requirement is confirmed; do not claim an RFP or promise meeting/catering capacity.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: May 2027 is an active announced edition with public registration and a named departmental inquiry channel. Hotel sales access is unconfirmed: attendee registration being open does not mean accommodation procurement is open. Do not label lodging as either available for bidding or committed elsewhere.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional strategy only: qualify the 2027 accommodation decision before proposing rates. No verified recurrence or later edition supports a recurring competitive-capture designation. If 2027 housing is already arranged, seek permission to support uncovered needs and develop the departmental relationship for separately verified future events, not an assumed annual FMF200.
